sentences.text:
Suresh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:6635
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 11th Of March, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 10505 of 2025
 Suresh
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Nimesh Pathak, learned counsel for the applicant
 Shri Viraj Godha, learned Public Prosecutor for the r
 Order

This second bail application under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicant Suresh for grant of regular bail,
who has been arrested on 16.02.2024 in connection with Crime No.46/2024 registered at Police Station Raipuriya, Dist. Jhabua (M.P.) for commission of offences under Section 376(1), 323 of IPC.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew the prayer after four months from today vide order dated 15.10.2024 passed in MCRC No.41240/2024.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the alleged date of incident is 08.02.2024 and FIR has been lodged on 09.02.2024 without any explanation.
Applicant is suffering incarceration since 16.02.2024 i.e. more than one year.
He further submits that there was previous enmity between the parties on the ground of Medh.
There is no sufficient evidence available on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6635 2 MCRC-10505-2025 record to establish the complicity of the accused with the alleged crime.
Investigation is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family, home and profession and also there is no likelihood of tampering with evidence by applicant.
Final conclusion of the trial will take considerable long time, therefore, learned counsel prays for allowing the bail application and for grant of bail.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State has vehemently opposed the prayer on the ground that in the statement under Section 164 CRPC, victim has supported the prosecution case and one bruise has been found on the back of the prosecutrix and prays for dismissal of the bail application.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

sentences.text: 5 . In the aforesaid factual backdrop, looking to the incarceration period, completion of investigation and also taking into consideration the fact that the trial is not going to conclude in near future, this Court is inclined to grant benefit of bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with separate solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by the said Court, without any default, during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.

7. The applicant will not indulge himself in any criminal activity in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6635 3 MCRC-10505-2025 future.

This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump and / or breach of any of the conditions of bail, this order will come to an end and applicant will be liable to be arrested by the concerned authorities.
8. The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
9. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
